title: Fixed-degree line quotients classify maps to a standard-open union of Proj
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}A_j$ be any nonnegatively graded commutative unital ring, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], and $d\geq1$. Set $U_d=\bigcup_{a\in A_d}D_+(a)\subseteq P$. Write $\mathcal O_P(j)$ for the twisting modules and $a$ for their canonical homogeneous sections [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. The restriction $M_d=\mathcal O_P(d)|_{U_d}$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], and multiplication identifies $M_d^{\otimes k}$ with $\mathcal O_P(kd)|_{U_d}$ for all $k\geq0$. The canonical homogeneous sections define a graded unital map $\eta^d:A^{(d)}\to\Gamma_*(U_d,M_d)$, where $A^{(d)}_k=A_{kd}$ and $\Gamma_*$ is [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. For any scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], invertible module $L$ on $T$, and graded unital ring map $\varphi:A^{(d)}\to\Gamma_*(T,L)$ such that the sections $\varphi(A_d)$ generate $L$ as a sheaf, there is a unique pair $(g,\alpha)$ consisting of a morphism $g:T\to U_d$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:g^*M_d\simeq L$ [def-pc-module-pullback] satisfying $\alpha^{\otimes k}(g^*\eta^d_k(b))=\varphi_k(b)$ for every $k\geq0$ and $b\in A_{kd}$. Conversely pullback of $(M_d,\eta^d)$ along any $g:T\to U_d$ has these properties. For $a\in A_d$ put $s=\varphi_1(a)$ and let $T_s$ be its nonvanishing open [def-sc-section-generating-locus]. The map has $g^{-1}D_+(a)=T_s$, and on this open its ring map sends $b/a^k$ to $\varphi_k(b)/s^{\otimes k}$ for $b\in A_{kd}$; division uses the free generator $s^{\otimes k}$. No generation hypothesis on $A$ and no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $T$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $V_a=D_+(a)$ for $a\in A_d$. Apply [lem-trf-proj-product-chart-twist-frame] with its $a=a$, $b=1$, $\beta=0$, and $n=k\geq1$: on every subopen of $V_a$, the section $a^k$ freely generates $\mathcal O_P(kd)$, and the coefficient of a homogeneous $b\in A_{kd}$ is $b/a^k$. For $k=0$ use $\mathcal O_P(0)=\mathcal O_P$. The twists are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists](c); their local rank-one frames show $M_d$ is invertible. Construct the multiplication maps by the bilinear fraction rule $(u/f^r,v/f^s)\mapsto uv/f^{r+s}$ on standard opens, using [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. The rule respects restrictions since the restrictions are localization homomorphisms. Extend it from the standard-open basis by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] and then use [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. On $V_a$ it sends $(r a^i)\otimes(t a^j)$ to $rt a^{i+j}$. Thus its inverse in these frames is $r a^{i+j}\mapsto(r a^i)\otimes a^j$. Restriction of tensor products is identified by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-tensor-comparison]; these local inverses agree because they invert the same multiplication map, and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1). Consequently multiplication gives $M_d^{\otimes k}\simeq\mathcal O_P(kd)|_{U_d}$ for all $k\geq0$. Associativity, commutativity and the unit follow in each frame from the corresponding scalar identities.

source.place: Tag 01MS (lemma-when-invertible), proof; equation-Ud and the paragraph before equation-psi-d.

proof.text: Restrict the canonical homogeneous sections of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] to $U_d$ and use step 1 to obtain $\eta^d_k:A_{kd}\to\Gamma(U_d,M_d^{\otimes k})$. On $V_a$ this sends $b$ to $(b/a^k)a^{\otimes k}$. The formulas $(b/a^i)(c/a^j)=bc/a^{i+j}$, additivity, and $1/1=1$ show that these maps form a graded unital ring map to the section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]; the equalities hold globally because sections agree on this cover. The images of $A_d$ generate $M_d$, since $a$ is a free generator on $V_a$. For any $c\in A_d$, its coefficient on $V_a$ is $c/a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection], $V_a\cap D_+(c)$ is the unit locus of $(c/a)^d$, which equals the unit locus of $c/a$ (a power is invertible exactly when its base is). Thus the nonvanishing locus of $\eta^d_1(c)$ is precisely $D_+(c)$ inside $U_d$.

source.place: Equations equation-Ud and equation-psi-d, the global-generation paragraph, and Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), first and second paragraphs of proof.

proof.text:
Let $s_a=\varphi_1(a)$ and $W_a=T_{s_a}$. These opens cover $T$: at a point choose a local frame of $L$; the coefficients of the $s_a$ generate the unit ideal in the local ring, so at least one coefficient is a unit, since otherwise every finite linear combination lies in the maximal ideal. By [def-sc-section-generating-locus], $s_a$ freely generates $L$ on $W_a$. On this open define
$\rho_a:A_{(a)}\to\Gamma(W_a,\mathcal O_T)$ by $b/a^k\mapsto\varphi_k(b)/s_a^{\otimes k}$.
Here [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] says that all elements have such representatives. If $b/a^k=c/a^l$, [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives $a^N(a^l b-a^k c)=0$ for some $N$. Applying $\varphi$ gives $s_a^{N+l}\varphi_k(b)=s_a^{N+k}\varphi_l(c)$ in $L^{\otimes(N+k+l)}$. Divide by the free generator $s_a^{N+k+l}$ to obtain the equality of the proposed values. The same tensor-power identifications from [def-sc-invertible-section-ring] give addition by a common denominator, multiplication by multiplying numerators and denominators, and preservation of $1$ in degree zero. Thus $\rho_a$ is a well-defined unital ring map, without cancelling a possibly vanishing section outside $W_a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] and [def-pc-proj], it determines $g_a:W_a\to V_a$.

source.place: Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), first paragraph of proof; Tag 01I1 (schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine).

proof.text:
Fix $a,c\in A_d$, and put $s=s_a,t=s_c$. On $W_a$ the function $\rho_a(c/a)=t/s$ is a unit exactly on $W_a\cap W_c$. The affine inverse-image assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] and the chart-intersection formula [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] therefore give $g_a^{-1}(V_a\cap V_c)=W_a\cap W_c$; use again that a function and its $d$th power have the same unit locus. On this intersection $s\otimes t$ freely generates $L^{\otimes2}$. The same fraction-relation calculation as in step 3, now with denominator $ac$ and the even-degree restriction of $\varphi$, defines a ring map
$A_{(ac)}\to\Gamma(W_a\cap W_c,\mathcal O_T)$, $z/(ac)^n\mapsto\varphi_{2n}(z)/(s\otimes t)^{\otimes n}$.
The restriction from $A_{(a)}$ sends $b/a^k$ to $bc^k/(ac)^k$, whose image is $\varphi_k(b)t^{\otimes k}/(s\otimes t)^{\otimes k}=\varphi_k(b)/s^{\otimes k}$. The symmetric calculation gives the $c$-chart map. These are the actual restriction maps by [def-pc-proj]. A ring map out of $A_{(ac)}$ is determined by its composite with $A_{(a)}\to A_{(ac)}$: the image $c/a$ becomes a unit with inverse $a^2/(ac)$, and every element is $z/(ac)^n=(z/a^{2n})(a^2/(ac))^n$ with $z/a^{2n}\in A_{(a)}$. Hence the ring map $A_{(ac)}\to\Gamma(W_a\cap W_c,\mathcal O_T)$ of $g_a|_{W_a\cap W_c}:W_a\cap W_c\to V_a\cap V_c=\operatorname{Spec}A_{(ac)}$, whose composite with this restriction is $\rho_a$ followed by restriction, equals the displayed map; symmetrically for $g_c$ via $A_{(c)}$. The affine Hom bijection thus proves that $g_a$ and $g_c$ agree as scheme morphisms on the overlap. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to obtain $g:T\to U_d$. Since the $W_a$ cover $T$, the inverse-image formula already proved on each $W_a$ gives $g^{-1}D_+(c)=W_c$ globally.

source.place: Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), second paragraph of proof: the overlap square and its common ring map.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-proj-generated-pullback-frames] for $g:T\to P$ (the composite of step 4 with $U_d\hookrightarrow P$), $M=L$, and the generating sections $s_a$. Its hypotheses hold by the generation assumption and step 4. It supplies the two free generators $g^*a$ and $s_a$ on $W_a$, on every subopen. Define $\alpha_a$ by $r g^*a\mapsto r s_a$. On $W_a\cap W_c$ the relation $c=(c/a)a$ pulls back to $g^*c=\rho_a(c/a)g^*a=(t/s)g^*a$. Hence $\alpha_a(g^*c)=(t/s)s=t=\alpha_c(g^*c)$; since $g^*c$ freely generates there, the two module maps agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1), the $\alpha_a$ glue to $\alpha:g^*M_d\to L$. Their inverses agree on overlaps as well, and the same gluing statement gives a two-sided inverse. This constructs the required isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), definition of alpha_f and the final sentences of the second paragraph of proof.

proof.text:
For $b\in A_{kd}$, step 2 gives $\eta^d_k(b)=(b/a^k)a^{\otimes k}$ on $V_a$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], including its formula on pure tensor sections, to identify its pullback with $g_a^\sharp(b/a^k)(g^*a)^{\otimes k}$. Applying $\alpha^{\otimes k}$ and step 3 gives
$\alpha^{\otimes k}(g^*\eta^d_k(b))=(\varphi_k(b)/s_a^{\otimes k})s_a^{\otimes k}=\varphi_k(b)$
on $W_a$. For $k=0$ the formula is the scalar ring map $\rho_a(b)=\varphi_0(b)$, with the zeroth tensor powers identified with the structure sheaves. The sheaf axiom on the cover $W_a$ proves the equality globally, in every degree.

source.place: Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), first paragraph of proof: verification of the diagram omitted in the source.

proof.text: Suppose $(h,\beta)$ satisfies the required equalities. In a local frame of an invertible sheaf, a section is nonvanishing exactly when its coefficient is a unit; a local homomorphism of local rings preserves and reflects units. Pulling back the nonvanishing identity of step 2 therefore gives $h^{-1}D_+(a)=W_a$, because $\beta(h^*\eta^d_1(a))=s_a$. On $W_a$ pull back the identity $\eta^d_k(b)=(b/a^k)a^{\otimes k}$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. The degree-$k$ compatibility and the equality $\beta(h^*a)=s_a$ imply $h^\sharp(b/a^k)s_a^{\otimes k}=\varphi_k(b)$, so division by the frame forces $h^\sharp=\rho_a$. The affine Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] gives $h|_{W_a}=g_a$. Scheme-morphism gluing uniqueness gives $h=g$. Under that equality $\beta$ and $\alpha$ both send the free generator $g^*a$ to $s_a$ on every $W_a$, so module-map gluing uniqueness gives $\beta=\alpha$. This uses only an open cover, not a claim that the degree-$d$ standard opens form a basis.

source.place: Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), uniqueness paragraph, replacing its incorrect fixed-degree-basis assertion by affine-chart uniqueness.

proof.text: Conversely let $g:T\to U_d$ be any morphism and put $L=g^*M_d$. Pulling a free frame $a$ back over $g^{-1}V_a$ gives a free frame $g^*a$: in the tensor formula [def-pc-module-pullback], $r\otimes(ua)\mapsto r g^\sharp(u)$ identifies the pullback with the free rank-one module. Thus $L$ is invertible and the sections $g^*\eta^d_1(a)$ generate it, since these opens cover $T$. The tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] and its pure-tensor formula make pullback of $\eta^d$ a graded unital map to the section ring. With $\alpha$ the identity these data satisfy all degreewise equations. Step 7 recovers the given pair uniquely, and its local division calculation also gives the required chart fraction formula. These arguments allow arbitrary covers and include empty $T$ or $U_d$.
